title: Learning About Learning https://www.nctq.org/publications/Learning-About-Learning:-What-Every-New-Teacher-Needs-to-Know
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), December 18, 2024 — original paper:
summary: This page summarizes an NCTQ report examining how well teacher-preparation programs align their textbooks and coursework with research-based instructional strategies. The report finds a large gap between six evidence-based practices identified by the Institute of Education Sciences and what trainee teachers are actually taught, with strategies like pairing graphics with words, linking abstract and concrete concepts, and distributing practice largely missing or poorly covered. Barton's summary frames this as a systemic training failure rather than an individual-teacher failure: new teachers are not being equipped with the tools cognitive science says work. The report calls on textbook authors, publishers, teacher-preparation programs, and state agencies to close the gap, arguing that low research standards in the field and a preference for individualized teaching philosophies over universally effective methods are partly to blame. For classroom teachers already in post, the takeaway is to seek out and self-apply these six strategies rather than assume they were covered in initial training.
points: Six evidence-based strategies from the Institute of Education Sciences are largely absent from the textbooks and coursework used to train new teachers, leaving a systemic gap rather than an individual one.
New teachers should be assessed frequently and given feedback on their errors, and should practice retrieving information from memory as a deliberate strategy, not an afterthought.
Teacher-preparation programs' preference for individualized teaching philosophies over universally effective methods is identified as part of why these strategies are under-taught.

Teachers can use a lesson-planning template to deliberately build in the six fundamental strategies regardless of subject or grade level, rather than relying on preparation programs to have installed them.
quotes: This report from the National Council on Teacher Quality assesses the alignment of teacher preparation programs' textbooks and coursework with research-based instructional strategies.
It finds a significant gap between established best practices, identified by the Institute of Education Sciences, and what is actually taught to aspiring teachers.

Teachers should use research-proven instructional strategies in their classrooms. The Institute of Education Sciences (IES) has identified six strategies that are supported by a large body of research.
Teachers need to understand the cognitive science behind learning. These strategies are based on an understanding of how the brain learns and retains information.
Teacher training programs need to do a better job of preparing teachers to use these strategies.
Teaching aspiring teachers how to maximize student learning and retention is the paramount task of their training.
